title: Your 2025-26 Smart Classroom Management Report Card port-card/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin offers an end-of-year self-assessment tool designed to give teachers a concrete picture of how closely they followed SCM principles during the school year. The exercise asks teachers to rate themselves from one to five on 15 core SCM practices, ranging from consistently following a classroom management plan and enforcing consequences calmly, to refraining from intimidation, praising only truly worthy effort, and maintaining low personal stress. The concrete technique is a belt-ranking system modeled on martial arts, converting the summed score into a rank from white belt up through the newly introduced 'red belt,' which he defines as true mastery where whatever classroom management excellence a teacher can imagine becomes their daily reality. The underlying argument is that self-honest reflection against a specific, itemized standard is what allows a teacher to identify precisely where to improve, and that reaching this level is achievable for any teacher who starts strong on day one.
points: The 15-item checklist covers concrete behaviors, not vague goals, such as enforcing consequences 'like a referee' and eschewing external rewards for intrinsic motivation.
Scores convert into a belt-rank system from white belt through black belt, with a new 'red belt' added to represent true mastery.
Red belt mastery means that whatever classroom management excellence a teacher can imagine becomes their actual daily teaching experience.
Linsin frames the report card as attainable for any teacher, provided they commit to starting strong on the first day of school.
quotes: At the end of every school year we post a report card for teachers. The purpose is to assess the degree you were able to follow the principles of Smart Classroom Management.
The way it works is that you’ll rate yourself on a scale of one to five—five being best—for each of 15 core SCM principles.
Black belt is excellent and a wonderful goal. However, I added the rank of red belt because it represents a true master.
That is, whatever classroom management excellence you can imagine becomes your daily teaching experience.
The good news is that it’s doable for anyone. The key is to start strong the first day of school.
